
`ampseqQC` turns the outputs of the [Mad4hatter](https://github.com/EPPIcenter/mad4hatter) pipeline and a sample manifest into an HTML QC report, with pass, repool and reprep calls for every sample.

**[See an example report](../example-report/QC_report.html)**.

## Install

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("EPPIcenter/ampseq-qc")
```

You also need the [Quarto CLI](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) to render the report.

## What you need

1. The **results directory** from Mad4hatter.
2. A **sample manifest** (comma or semicolon separated) with one row per well and the columns:

| Column | Contents |
| ------ | -------- |
| `sample_name` | Sample name, matching the names given to Mad4hatter |
| `SampleType` | `sample`, `positive` or `negative` |
| `Batch` | The plate or batch the sample was processed in |
| `Column` | Plate column |
| `Row` | Plate row |
| `Parasitemia` | qPCR parasitemia |

## Render the report

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(ampseqQC)

render_qc_report(
  results_dir = "path/to/mad4hatter/results",
  manifest_file = "path/to/manifest.csv",
  output_dir = "qc_output"
)
```

Or from the command line:

```bash
Rscript -e 'ampseqQC::render_qc_report("path/to/results", "path/to/manifest.csv", output_dir = "qc_output")'
```

To try it on the example run included with the package:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
tutorial_dir <- system.file("extdata", "tutorial", package = "ampseqQC")

render_qc_report(
  results_dir = file.path(tutorial_dir, "results"),
  manifest_file = file.path(tutorial_dir, "manifest.csv"),
  output_dir = "qc_output"
)
```

`qc_output` will contain `QC_report.html` and the QC tables, including `samples_to_repool.csv`, `samples_to_reprep.csv` and `reprep_repool_summary.csv`.

## Change the settings

Thresholds and other settings are arguments to `render_qc_report()`. For example, to change the reads needed for a target to count as amplified and the reprep threshold:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
render_qc_report(
  results_dir = "path/to/mad4hatter/results",
  manifest_file = "path/to/manifest.csv",
  output_dir = "qc_output",
  read_threshold = 50,
  reprep_threshold = 0.4
)
```

All of the settings and their defaults are listed on the [`render_qc_report()` reference page](../reference/render_qc_report.html), or with `?render_qc_report` in R.

The report works out which pools were run from the Mad4hatter panel information. The MAD4HatTeR and PfPHAST pools are mapped to their mPCR reactions by default; for other pools or a different reaction layout, see [`panel_settings()`](../reference/panel_settings.html).

## Going further

To run the QC steps yourself or build your own summaries, see [Building a custom QC with the package functions](custom-qc.html).
